title: Modi Calls for Unity Against Divisive Forces at Chinmaya Sammelan Inauguration
excerpt: Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to tackle new challenges, embrace self-reliance and commit to a developed India by 2047.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the three-day Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on October 23, marking 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission.
  • Modi called on citizens to unite society against divisive forces, tackle new societal challenges and distortions, and inspire every individual toward self-reliance.
  • He linked the Mission's work to the Viksit Bharat 2047 goal, noting India's centenary of independence in 2047 will coincide with the Chinmaya Mission's centenary year.
  • More than 9,000 participants from India and abroad are attending the October 23-25 gathering, the culmination of year-long celebrations that began in 2025.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday called for efforts to address emerging societal ills and new challenges, unite society against divisive forces and inspire citizens towards self-reliance, inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.

Modi said the Chinmaya Mission was not merely an institution but a thought. Chinmaya, meaning pure consciousness, was founded by a sage whose journey over the decades had been marked by divine resolves, he said, according to reports of the address.

"We must unite society against the forces that seek to divide us. We must make our citizens aware and inspired towards self-reliance. We must connect every individual with the resolve of a Developed India by 2047."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India

A Shared Responsibility

"In the past decades, times have changed, new challenges have emerged before the country, and new societal ills have surfaced. Today, the responsibility of solving them rests upon all of us," Modi said. He added that for these objectives, "we must become even more proactive."

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2113505098794230187

The prime minister said the nation was the birthplace of Indian culture and the foundation of the country's existence. Citing the Vedic mantra "Vayam Rashtra Jagruyam Purohitaah," he said it called on people to work towards making the nation aware and advanced, and that Swami Chinmayananda had lived his entire life guided by that mantra.

"This nation is the foundation of our existence. Swami Ji always taught us to connect our spiritual progress with personal advancement, and to make personal advancement a medium for the nation's progress," Modi said, in remarks carried by ANI's report of the address. Instilling self-respect for India among its people was central to Chinmayananda's mission, he added.

Amrit Mahotsav as a Springboard

Modi also outlined the philosophy behind declaring India's 75th year of independence as Amrit Mahotsav. "As we approached the 75th anniversary of our nation's independence, I envisioned this occasion not only as a springboard for a 'Viksit Bharat' but also as an opportunity to revive that essence of India which embraces 'Amrit' ideals — an India that, drawing upon the wisdom of countless centuries, remains deeply committed to the well-being of humanity across the ages," he said, in the fuller text published by News On Radar India.

He praised spiritual, cultural and social organisations for adopting "Amrit Sankalps" at milestones in their own journeys, and said the Chinmaya Mission had now joined that national endeavour as part of Amrit Mahotsav.

Youth, Heritage and Education

Modi said millions of young people were working as cultural brand ambassadors of India thanks to the Mission's efforts, carrying Indian values to a new generation. He noted that young members of the Chinmaya Yuva Kendra had travelled 40,000 kilometres over about 300 days during the celebrations, reaching more than one lakh young people.

He recalled a personal interaction with Swami Chinmayananda in 1993, saying an interaction with a holographic projection of the spiritual leader at the event made him feel transported 33 years back in time. He also pointed to the National Education Policy as an effort to align modern education with India's knowledge traditions, mother-tongue instruction, modern science and new technology.

75 Years of the Chinmaya Mission

The three-day Sammelan, held from October 23 to 25, brings together over 9,000 participants from India and abroad. It marks the culmination of year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951 to make the wisdom of Vedanta and the Bhagavad Gita accessible to all.

The year-long celebrations included a Chinmaya Amrit Yatra, mass havans, the consecration of a temple in Tripura, and a global online chanting of the 15th chapter of the Bhagavad Gita by more than one lakh people. Modi noted that in 2047, when India marks 100 years of independence, the Chinmaya Mission will also be in its centenary year, and said the two journeys share the same goal and must move forward together.
